title: Kitebridge - inference stability and cost rightsize sync
summary: Quick QBR-style checkin focused on recent latency spikes during peak traffic, cost drivers from embedding usage, and options for rightsizing Dedicated capacity vs staying Hosted with smarter batching and caching. Agreed to run a 72-hour benchmark on Dedicated configuration and share security/compliance docs for VPC peering. Follow-ups: benchmark results, pricing tier writeup, and a joint runbook for failover between Hosted and Dedicated.
topics: Recent incident postmortem and latency spikes
Cost breakdown: embeddings vs generation and token distribution
VPC peering and security docs (SOC2 + SSO/SAML)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-16 15:00 PDT | Duration 48m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Kitebridge CTO), Maya (SRE), Sam (PM)
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to do a quick health sync, go over the spike last week, and talk rightsizing options. Priya will jump into the perf measurements.
[00:18] Jordan: yeah hi, thanks. quick context - we saw tail latency jump at 11:30am on tuesday during the new onboarding flow release. user facing page loads slowed and we had a few retries from the frontend.
[00:31] Maya: and we saw a corresponding increase in embedding calls - a tonne of short embeddings for search vectors, probably due to the background job.
[00:45] Priya: hmm ok, do we have breakdowns by model and sequence length? sometimes the seq length distribution trips the kernel selection and batching heuristics.
[00:59] Sam: I put a quick spreadsheet in the chat - main spike was with gen-model-rw1 at 2k seq for multi-turn support, embeddings were using emb-2-small heavily.
[01:12] Alex: got it. so two axes - generation cost and latency, plus embedding throughput. on the host side are you on hosted or dedicated currently?
[01:20] Jordan: hosted API, with some reserved capacity for peak windows but not Dedicated pools. we were considering Dedicated but worried about commit size.
[01:33] Priya: right, Dedicated can give a predictable tail latency but you trade commit and utilization. there are also middle options - autoscale policies, burst capacity, and tuning batching + prefix KV cache.
[01:46] Maya: can you explain KV cache? we hear that term in docs but not sure how much lift it is to enable.
[01:54] Priya: sure - KV (key value) cache stores recent attention key/values for reused contexts, reduces repeated compute for similar prefixes. for chat-heavy flows it can drop per-token latency quite a bit but it has memory implications. also prefix caching is different - caches start-of-conversation embeddings and can avoid regen.
[02:18] Jordan: okay makes sense. the other ask from our security team was around VPC peering and audit logs - we need SOC2 artifact and SAML integration docs.
[02:28] Alex: yeah we'll share the SOC2 report and the SAML/SSO guide. Redwood Private also supports customer-controlled KMS for keys if needed.
[02:36] Sam: on cost - embeddings are the big line in the invoice. do you have quick wins to reduce embedding volume?
[02:43] Priya: commonly we see unnecessary fresh embeddings - you can cache vectors for 24-48 hours for some workloads, delta-updates instead of full re-embed, or move to batched embedding calls rather than one-per-document. also model choice: emb-2-small vs emb-2-large trade accuracy vs cost.
[03:05] Maya: our pipeline re-embeds every time a doc is edited; we could change that to only re-embed changed chunks.
[03:12] Jordan: what's the recommended pilot to validate Dedicated? if we do Dedicated for two pools (inference and embeddings) how long to run a meaningful test?
[03:21] Priya: usually 48-72 hours of representative traffic gives us enough signal for latency and cost-per-token under peak. we can synthetic replay if you want to avoid production risk.
[03:31] Alex: + we'll instrument token-level cost and latency tracing so you can see per-route breakdowns.
[03:38] Sam: ok, timeline wise we'd like results before our Nov budget meeting, so end of October would be ideal.
[03:46] Priya: that works. we'll draft a pilot plan: config options (dedicated GPU types, autoscale floor, burst cap), synthetic replay config, and what metrics we collect.
[03:57] Jordan: quick question - if Dedicated is underutilized we'll still pay the commit. any autoscale to reduce bill?
[04:05] Priya: Dedicated has autoscale policies and burst capacity. you can set a guaranteed baseline to keep tail latency predictable, then allow bursting to hosted pool. there's also recommendation engine in Redwood Optimize to suggest right-sizing based on historical token patterns.
[04:22] Maya: earlier you mentioned kernel selection issues - can mis-selection cause spikes?
[04:27] Priya: yes, if the runtime picks an inefficent kernel for a longer seq length distribution, that can bump latency. our runtime re-evaluates kernel choice periodically; on big distribution shifts we recommend a warmup run after deployment so kernels and memory layouts stabilize.
[04:45] Jordan: got it. any immediate mitigation if we see spikes again tomorrow?
[04:50] Alex: short-term: reduce batch windows, enable stricter latency SLO routing which will route some requests to cheaper but lower-cap models, and enable prefix caching for repeated flows. medium: pilot Dedicated.
[05:02] Sam: about rollout - if we do canary, can Redwood do automatic fallback to hosted? we want graceful degradation during failures.
[05:10] Priya: yes, Redwood supports canary + auto-fallback policies that will send traffic back to hosted variants if errors or latency breach thresholds.
[05:21] Maya: what about data residency? some EU users need data never to leave region.
[05:26] Alex: we have region pinning and Private deployment options for VPC/on-prem. we can provide a timeboxed pilot within eu-west to validate.
[05:36] Jordan: ok let's talk concrete next steps.
[05:39] Alex: action items and owners - we'll capture in notes but also defer to the follow-up email.
[05:45] Priya: i'll propose a pilot config doc and schedule a 72-hour replay window, include the kernel warmup and baseline metrics.
[05:55] Sam: i'll surface this in the product roadmap and ensure engineering gives a stable traffic window late october.
[06:01] Maya: security will review SOC2 and SAML docs - expecting them by EOD tomorrow?
[06:06] Alex: yes we'll send security pack and KMS options by COB tomorrow.
[06:11] Jordan: pricing - can you share a cost projection for Dedicated vs optimized Hosted for the pilot?
[06:17] Alex: yes, we'll send a pricing tier writeup with estimated daily token burn and 30/60/90 day scenarios.
[06:24] Priya: also including common tuning knobs: batch size, batching latency windows, prefix cache TTL, and embedding cache heuristics.
[06:33] Sam: anything else on reliability? we also want a joint failover playbook.
[06:38] Alex: we'll propose a 1-page runbook for failover and escalation contacts.
[06:43] Jordan: ok thanks.
[06:45] Alex: cool, we'll follow up with the doc links. thanks everyone.
[06:50] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "gen-model-rw1" might be transcribed as "gen model new one" in raw export, and some acronyms like KMS, KV appear as K-M-S, K-V in places.
